intro.bio: I'm a Frontier Commons fellow learning to build software. This week I'm working through the Build Bootcamp with Claude Code, GitHub and Vercel.

items.name: Cadgy clone
items.summary: A working rebuild of OneLook's Cadgy, a daily word-tile puzzle: pick one tile per column to spell words. It has accounts, a one-click guest login, a create form where Gemini suggests the word list, and a leaderboard for every puzzle.

items.name: Personal finance tracker
items.stack: Google Apps Script · Gemini · Claude Code
items.summary: Tracking money by hand was cumbersome, and the apps I tried cost money without doing what I wanted. Bank alert emails from UOB, PayLah, ShopBack, Grab and others are parsed and categorised automatically into a review tab. Once ticked, they flow into income or expenses and a monthly summary. Cash receipts can be sent in as photos.

items.name: Tailored fitness app
items.summary: For beginners, or people getting back into fitness, who find tutorials and existing apps too impersonal. A chatbot asks questions that build on each other: your health, history, goals, experience and habits. It then produces a personal site with a phased plan, a workout calendar and a log that you can edit.

items.name: FC-Bootcamp
items.summary: The repo for my run through the Frontier Commons Build Bootcamp: four weeks of material in about 36 hours. It holds this site, the clone, and the PRD and planning docs that scoped them.

entries.note: Wrote the PRD, the rules and the schema before any code, so every later change had a contract to check against.
Picked Cadgy for the clone. It had nothing for users to create, so I turned it into players submitting puzzles, with me as editor of the dailies.
create-next-app took six minutes, almost all of it npm install. Now I start installs in the background and do the dashboard steps while they run.
Every Supabase table gets RLS and an explicit policy in the same change that creates it, so a second account can't touch what the first one made.
